name: Nestorius
major_ideas: The Nestorian controversy (two Persons vs. one)
biography: Patriarch of Constantinople who held that Christ's human and divine natures constituted two distinct Persons, and objected on this ground to calling the Virgin 'Mother of God'; condemned as a heretic at the Council of Ephesus (431), founding the Nestorian sect that spread through Syria, Persia, India, and eventually China.
central_doctrines: The Nestorian controversy (two Persons vs. one): The Christological dispute, chiefly between Nestorius and Cyril, over whether Christ's divinity and humanity constitute two distinct Persons (Nestorius's view) or are united in a single Person, and, if united, whether in one nature or two.
